stem: An agriculture study measures crop yield across 3 regions, each containing multiple farms. region A has 8 observations with mean 70.2 tonnes/hectare (within-region SD = 8.4). region B has 15 observations with mean 64.5 tonnes/hectare (within-region SD = 8.5). region C has 10 observations with mean 53.6 tonnes/hectare (within-region SD = 5.4). The between-region standard deviation is uncertain, estimated between 7.9 and 19.8 tonnes/hectare. Using a hierarchical Bayesian model, estimate the true crop yield for region A, accounting for shrinkage toward the grand mean and the uncertainty in the between-region variation.

ground_truth.answer: Hierarchical estimate for region A: 69.8 tonnes/hectare (shrunk from raw 70.2). Range [69.3, 70.0] as between-region SD varies from 7.9 to 19.8. Pooled mean: 62.6.

solution_steps: Compute pooled (grand) mean: 62.6 tonnes/hectare (weighted average of 3 region means).
Shrinkage factor for region A: B = σ²_between / (σ²_between + σ²_within/8). At σ_between=13.2: B = 0.952.
Interval [69.3, 70.0] captures uncertainty from the unknown between-group variance.
common_failure_modes: Using the raw observed mean (70.2) without shrinkage
Using only the grand mean (62.6) and ignoring group-specific data
Not recognizing that small-sample groups should be shrunk more toward the grand mean
Treating the between-group variance as known rather than uncertain
